Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D.
Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

Section II Reading Comprehension

Part A

Text 1

The assumption that remote work would reduce the demand for office space rested on a simple
calculation. If employees work from home three days a week, the argument ran, a firm needs
only sixty per cent of the desks it once maintained. That reasoning has proved remarkably
resilient in the boardroom and remarkably fragile in practice. Firms that reduced their
footprint discovered that attendance is not evenly distributed across the week. Almost
everyone appears on the same days, and on those days the remaining desks are insufficient,
while on other days whole floors stand empty. The consequence is a peculiar kind of
inefficiency, in which a company pays for space it does not use and still fails to provide
space when it is needed. Planners have proposed a further implication: that the office should
be reconceived not as a place where work is performed but as a place where a particular kind
of work is performed. Collaborative tasks, the argument goes, benefit disproportionately from
physical proximity, while concentrated individual work does not. If that distinction holds,
the relevant question is not how many days employees should attend, but which activities
justify the journey. Some executives remain sceptical, observing that the evidence for the
collaboration benefit is thinner than its advocates suggest. Nevertheless the debate has
moved on. Few now dispute that the office must justify its cost, and that is itself a
considerable shift.

[A] To explain why remote work has become popular.
[B] To show that a plausible calculation can fail in practice.
[C] To prove that offices are no longer necessary.

22. The word "resilient" (Line 3) most probably means ______.
